result.journal: Proc. ACM Interact. Mob. Wearable Ubiquitous Technol.
result.keywords: Mobile virtual reality (VR) applications increasingly combine sensor-driven interaction with networked content delivery, creating complex traffic patterns in LTE environments. In this fictional study, we examine how Android VR apps disclose motion, scene, and telemetry data over cellular links and ask whether their network requests can reveal the underlying data collection and rendering purposes. We propose NetVR-Purpose, a client-side analysis pipeline that uses URL naming cues, payload structure, and device-side context to infer why a request is sent, while also assessing the latency impact of signaling and offloading in operational 4G LTE networks. Our evaluation blends controlled app traces with expert labeling to classify traffic into multiple purpose categories and quantify the tradeoff between privacy transparency and interactive VR performance. We discuss implications for edge-assisted mobile VR and future 5G deployments.
result.title: Inferring Mobile VR Traffic Purposes in LTE Apps: A Cross-Layer Study
